L.te: What Do You Want to Eat?
L.su: Two friends decide what to have for lunch.
ss: Are you hungry?
I'm very hungry. What do you want to eat?
I want rice and eggs.
I don't want rice; I want noodles.
OK, let's go to that restaurant.
What will you drink?
I'll have water. And you?
I'll have tea.
g: I want to go to school.
吧 at the end of a sentence makes a suggestion.
q: What does Xiao Li want to eat?

L.su: A girl tells us who is in her family.
ss: There are five in my family: Dad, Mum, my older brother, me and the little dog.
Dad is a doctor; he works at the hospital.
Mum is a teacher; she is very busy.
My brother is eighteen this year; he is a university student.
I am ten this year and study at primary school.
The little dog is small and also very cute.
I love my family.
q: How many people are in the family?

L.su: A short note about the weather this week.
ss: The weather is very nice today; there are no clouds in the sky.
It will rain tomorrow and be a bit cold.
The day after tomorrow it won't rain, and we'll go to the shop to buy things.
I'm not at home today; I'm at school.
Look, that is my friend.
His name is Xiao Gao, and he is tall.
g: 不 + verb or adjective makes a negative.

L.su: Buying a hat in a small shop.
ss: Boss, how much is this?
This one is fifty yuan.
Too expensive. What about that one?
That one is thirty yuan, and it's new.
I'll take that one.
OK, thank you.
You're welcome. Goodbye!
Goodbye!
g: 要 can mean "to want; to take".
I want a glass of water.
q: How much is the first hat?
What does Xiaomei say to end?

L.su: A passenger tells the driver where to go.
ss: Hello, where are you going?
I'm going to the train station. Please drive a bit faster.
There are many cars on the road now. It will take twenty minutes.
That's all right. My train doesn't leave until nine.
Is this your first time in Beijing?
No, I came last year.
We're here. It's twenty-five yuan in total.
Here you are. Thank you, goodbye!
g: 去 + place means "go to a place".
Verb + 过 means "have done it before".
q: Where does Tom want to go?
How long will the trip take?

L.su: Xiaomei orders a coffee and some bread.
ss: Hello! What would you like to drink?
I'd like a cup of coffee.
Do you want a large or a small cup?
A small one, thank you.
Would you like something to eat?
I'd like a piece of bread.
That's twenty-five yuan altogether.
Here is the money for you.
Thank you! Please have a seat.
Thank you!
g: 想 means "would like to" and is polite. 要 is more direct and is common when ordering: "I'll have…".
还是 means "or" when you offer a choice in a question.
Do you want tea or coffee?
一共 means "altogether" and is used when adding up a price.
A question word such as 什么 simply takes the place of the answer. The word order does not change.
What would you like to drink?
q: What size coffee does Xiaomei order?

L.su: Friends sing and give gifts at a birthday party.
ss: Hello, everyone! Today is my birthday.
Happy birthday! This is a gift for you.
Thank you! Is it a book?
Yes. Don't you like reading?
Come, let's have cake. Would you like a big piece or a small one?
I'd like a big one.
How old are you this year?
I'm eleven. And you?
I am twelve today.
g: A question with 是……吗 asks whether something is true.
还是 means "or" in a question that gives a choice.
Do you drink tea or coffee?

L.su: A girl shows a family photo to her friend.
ss: Xiaomei, who is this?
This is my father, and this is my mother.
Who is this little child?
He is my younger brother. He is five years old this year.
How many people are there in your family?
Five: father, mother, older brother, younger brother, and me.
Where does your older brother work?
He works at a hospital. He is a doctor.
g: 家有几口人？ asks how many people are in a family. 口 is the measure word for family members.
There are four people in my family.
在 + place goes before the verb to say where something happens.
q: How old is Xiaomei's younger brother?
How many people are in Xiaomei's family?
What does Xiaomei's older brother do?

L.te: What Would You Like to Eat?
L.su: Two people order lunch in a restaurant.
ss: Hello, please sit down. What would you like to eat?
I would like rice and chicken.
What would you like to drink?
I'll have a cup of tea. My friend will have a glass of water.
All right, please wait a moment.
Sorry, I didn't order this dish.
Oh, I'm sorry. I'll take it away right away.
It's okay. The food is delicious, thank you!
g: 想 before a verb means "would like to" or "want to".
I would like to drink tea.
Say 对不起 to say sorry, and 没关系 to answer "it doesn't matter".
q: What does Mark want to eat?
What was wrong with the dish?

L.su: A mother and son talk about the week.
ss: Mum, what day is it today?
Today is Saturday.
Great! I don't have school.
Tomorrow is Sunday. What do you want to do?
I want to go and see a film with my friends.
What time are you going?
Two in the afternoon. I'll be home at six.
OK, come back early.
g: 几 asks for a small number: "how many" or "which (day/time)".
和 A 一起 means "together with A".
I go to read with a friend.
q: What does the son want to do?

L.su: Two friends check the time before school.
ss: Xiaohong, what time is it now?
It is half past seven now.
Oh! Class starts at eight. Let's hurry.
Don't worry, the school is very close.
Did you eat breakfast?
Yes. I ate an egg and a piece of bread.
I didn't eat. I'm very hungry now.
I have an apple. Here you go.
Thank you!
g: Ask the time with 几点 (what hour). Answer with number + 点.
了 after a verb shows the action is finished.
q: What did Xiaohong eat for breakfast?

L.su: A boy introduces himself, his age and his city.
ss: My name is Wang Ming.
I am Chinese.
I am twelve years old this year.
I live in Beijing.
I am a student, and I study at Beijing No. 1 Middle School.
My teacher's surname is Li.
I like my school, and I like my teacher too.
What is your name?
g: 是 (shì) means "to be". Use it to say who or what someone is.
住在 + place tells where you live.

L.su: Xiaomei and David meet for the first time and introduce themselves.
ss: Hello! My name is Xiaomei.
Hello, Xiaomei! My name is David.
Which country are you from?
I'm American. And you?
I'm Chinese.
Are you a student?
Yes, I'm a student. Are you also a student?
No, I'm a teacher.
Nice to meet you!
Nice to meet you too!
g: 是 (shì) works like "to be" and links two nouns. Say 不是 for "am/is/are not".
Put 吗 at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. The word order stays the same.
也 means "also" and goes right before the verb.
呢 bounces a question back to the other person, like "And you?"
q: What does 吗 do at the end of a sentence?

L.su: A short description of a family of four and their cat.
ss: There are four people in my family.
Dad, mom, my older brother and me.
My dad is a doctor.
My mom is a teacher.
My older brother is twenty this year. He is a university student.
We also have a little cat at home.
It is very cute.
I love my family.
g: 有 (yǒu) means "to have", and also "there is / there are".
Chinese puts a measure word between a number and a noun. 口 is used for family members and 只 for small animals.
Add 的 after a pronoun to show ownership. For close family, 的 is often left out: 我爸爸 "my dad".
Adjectives in plain statements normally take 很 in front. It is often weak and does not always mean "very".
q: How many people are in the family?
What does the older brother do?
What pet does the family have?

L.su: A customer buys apples and asks about the price.
ss: Boss, how much are the apples?
Five yuan per jin.
Too expensive. Three yuan, okay?
No, no. Make it four yuan.
All right. I want two jin.
Eight yuan in total.
Here is ten yuan.
Here's two yuan change. Goodbye!
Goodbye!
g: 太 + adjective + 了 means "too ..." or "so ...".
一共 means "altogether" and is used when you add up numbers.
q: How much does one jin of apples cost at first?
How many jin does the customer buy?
How much change does the customer get?

L.su: A busy worker describes a normal day from morning to bedtime.
ss: Every morning I get up at six thirty.
At seven I have breakfast. I often eat eggs and drink milk.
At eight I take the bus to work.
At noon I eat at a restaurant near the company.
I finish work at five in the afternoon.
After I get home, I cook, watch TV, and go to bed at eleven.
I feel that every day is busy, but I'm happy too.
g: Time words go before the verb
In Chinese, time words such as 七点 or 中午 come before the verb, usually right after the subject.
在 + place says where the action happens.
Put 以后 after a time or an action to say "after…".
但是 means "but" and introduces the contrasting part.
q: What time does the writer get up?
How does the writer get to work?
What does the writer often have for breakfast?

L.te: What I Did on the Weekend
L.su: A diary entry about a quiet weekend.
ss: The weather was lovely this weekend, and I went to the park with my family.
There were many people in the park; some were running and some were doing tai chi.
We sat by the lake for a while, and my father took many photos of me.
At noon we did not go home, but ate dumplings at a restaurant next to the park.
In the afternoon I went to a friend's home, and we did homework together.
In the evening I called my grandmother, and she said she missed me a lot.
I felt this weekend went by happily.
g: 有的 A，有的 B means "some do A, some do B".
有的人喝茶，有的人喝咖啡。
Some people drink tea, some drink coffee.
过得 + adjective describes how time or life is spent.
q: What did they eat at noon?
Who did the writer phone in the evening?

L.su: A child describes the family cat.
ss: I have a little cat, and it is white.
Its eyes are big and also pretty.
It likes to eat fish and doesn't like to drink water.
At noon it sleeps under the table.
In the evening it is with me.
I call it Xiaobai.
Xiaobai is my good friend.
g: 的 links a describing word to a noun, or shows possession.
喜欢 + noun or verb means "to like".
q: What does it like to eat?
Where does it sleep at noon?

L.su: Over dinner, Xiaomei asks David to put his phone away.
ss: Why do you keep looking at your phone? We're eating!
Sorry, I'm replying to a work email.
It's rest time now. Work can wait until tomorrow.
You're right. I've been too busy lately. As soon as my phone rings, I want to look.
I'm like that too. So now when I eat, I put my phone in my bag.
That's a good idea. I'll try it too.
Then let's chat for a while first today.
Okay. Anything new with you lately?
g: 怎么 can mean "how", but before a verb it often means "why / how come" and carries surprise or mild complaint.
How come you're not asleep yet?
在 before a verb shows the action is happening right now. 呢 at the end adds a "this is going on" feeling.
一 + verb … 就 + verb means "as soon as … then …".
As soon as he gets home, he sleeps.
再 means "again" or "(do it) later". It is used for future actions.
q: Why is Xiaomei unhappy with David?
He keeps looking at his phone during dinner
What is David doing on his phone?
What does Xiaomei do with her phone when she eats?
She puts it in her bag

L.su: A mother and her son decide what to wear.
ss: Xiaoming, look. It is raining outside.
Really? The weather was very good yesterday.
It is very cold today. You should wear a bit more.
I'm not cold. I don't want to wear this piece of clothing.
No. You will get sick.
Fine. Can I take my new umbrella?
Of course. Will the weather be good tomorrow?
I don't know. The TV says it will be sunny tomorrow.
g: 在 before a verb means the action is going on right now.
会 can also mean "will" when you guess what is going to happen.
q: What is the weather like today?
What does Xiaoming want to take?
What does the TV say about tomorrow?

L.su: Good manners when you visit a Chinese family.
ss: Welcome, welcome! Please come in. No need to take your shoes off.
Thank you. Here is some fruit I brought for you.
You're too polite. Just coming would be fine. Why bring anything?
In my country, you must bring a gift when you visit someone's home.
It's the same in China. Come on, have some tea first.
Your home is beautiful!
Not at all, it's very small. Dinner will be ready soon. Please wait a little longer.
Can I help you with anything?
No, you are a guest. Just sit and chat.
g: 哪里哪里 is a modest reply to a compliment.
A: 你汉语说得真好！ B: 哪里哪里。
A: You speak Chinese really well! B: Not at all.
Verb + 就 + Verb (+ 嘛) means "just do it, that is enough"; a remark that nothing more is needed often follows.
q: Is Mary required to take off her shoes?
What does Xiao Wang say when Mary praises his home?
Not at all, it's very small

L.su: A girl shows what is in her room.
ss: This is my room.
The room is not big, but it is very clean.
On the desk there is a computer and some books.
The bed is on the left of the desk, and the chair is in front of the desk.
Next to the window there is a pot of flowers, and the flowers are red.
On the wall there is a map.
I like my room very much because I can read and listen to music here.
g: Place words like 左边, 前面 and 旁边 follow the thing they relate to.
The book is to the left of the desk.
"Place + 有 + thing" says what is in a place.
There is a book on the desk.

L.te: What Shall We Do This Weekend?
L.su: Two friends plan a weekend walk in the park.
ss: Are you free this weekend?
Yes. What do you want to do?
I'd like to go for a walk in the park. The weather should be nice.
Sounds good! What time shall we meet?
Nine in the morning, at the entrance to the subway station.
Nine is too early. Is ten okay?
Okay. I'll bring fruit. What will you bring?
I'll bring my camera. We can take lots of photos.
That's great! See you at the weekend!
g: 几 (jǐ) asks "how many?" so 几点 asks "what time?". Answer with number + 点.
可以 means "may / can / is it okay to". It covers permission and possibility.
Repeating a verb (走走) makes the action short and relaxed: "just take a little walk".
q: What time do they decide on?

L.su: Two friends choose a film and a time.
ss: Xiaomei, there is a new film this weekend. Do you want to go?
What film? Is it an action movie?
No, it's a romance. I hear it's quite good.
Sure. What time does it start?
There are two shows: three in the afternoon and half past seven in the evening.
I have a piano lesson in the afternoon, so let's see the evening one.
OK. I'll buy tickets online right now.
Great. Before we watch the movie, let's eat first.
g: 是不是 asks the other person to confirm a guess.
以前 means "before" and 以后 means "after".
After eating I go for a walk.
q: What kind of film is it?
Why can't Xiaomei go in the afternoon?
How does David buy the tickets?

L.su: A student writes home from China.
ss: Dear Anna:
How are you? I have been in Beijing for a month already.
I live in a small house next to the school. It is not big but it is very quiet.
Every morning I go to Chinese class, and in the afternoon I chat with Chinese classmates.
They are very kind to me and often teach me to speak Chinese.
The food here is delicious. I like dumplings and noodles best.
If you have time, come and visit Beijing too!
I miss you.
Your friend, Mary
g: 已经 ... 了 shows something has already happened or reached a state.
的话 turns the part before it into "if".
If you are free, come to my place.
q: How long has Mary been in Beijing?
What does she invite Anna to do?

L.te: How Mobile Phones Changed Our Lives
L.su: An article about daily life with smartphones in China.
ss: Ten years ago many people still carried wallets when going out. Now a phone is enough.
Shopping, taking a bus and ordering food can all be paid for with a phone.
People also rarely go to the bank, because most things can be done online.
Many young people use their phones to read the news, listen to music and learn languages.
But phones have also brought some problems.
Some people look at their phones too long every day, which is bad for the eyes.
At meals everyone is often playing with their phones and not talking.
So experts advise us: leave yourself some "no-phone" time every day.
g: 只要 + thing + 就够了 means "as long as you have ... it's enough".
对 + object + adjective says whether something is good or bad for someone.
喝太多咖啡对身体不好。
Too much coffee is bad for the body.
q: What do people now carry when going out?
What problem does the article mention?
People spend too long on their phones
Leave some no-phone time every day

L.su: A short description of a busy Monday at school.
ss: On Monday I get up at seven.
I eat breakfast and go to school at eight.
In the morning we have three classes: Chinese, math and English.
At noon we eat at school.
In the afternoon there is one PE class and we play football.
I go home at four in the afternoon.
In the evening I do homework first, and then watch TV for a while.
g: 先 and 然后 put actions in order: first this, then that.
I eat first, then I read.
q: What time does the boy get up?
What class is there in the afternoon?
What does he do first in the evening?

L.su: A short description of the seasons in the Chinese capital.
ss: Beijing has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
Spring is neither too cold nor too hot, and the flowers in the parks are all in bloom.
Summer is very hot and often has heavy rain, but the evenings are comfortable.
Autumn is the best season in Beijing. The sky is very blue and the leaves are yellow.
Winter is very cold, and sometimes it snows.
When it snows, many people go and play at the Great Wall.
I like autumn best, because it is neither cold nor hot.
Which season do you like?
g: 不 A 也不 B means "neither A nor B".
I drink neither tea nor coffee.
Sometimes I take the subway to work.
q: Which season does the writer like best?
What colour are the leaves in autumn?
What do many people do when it snows?

L.su: A new student chats with a classmate about languages.
ss: Hello! Are you the new student?
Yes, my name is Mary, and I'm British.
Can you speak Chinese?
A little. I have studied for half a year.
You speak very well! Are Chinese characters difficult?
A bit difficult, but very interesting.
I can teach you, and you can teach me English.
Great! We are good friends now.
g: 会 means "can" for a skill you have learned.
有点儿 + adjective means "a bit" and is often used for something you don't quite like.
It is a bit cold today.
q: How long has Mary studied Chinese?
What does Mary say about Chinese characters?

L.su: A student asks an agent about a flat.
ss: Hello, I saw online that you have a two-bedroom flat for rent.
Yes, on the third floor, only five minutes from the subway station.
How much is it per month?
Four thousand five hundred. You pay for water and electricity yourself.
That's a bit expensive. Can it be a little cheaper?
If you rent for a year, I can take off five hundred yuan.
Is there furniture in the flat?
Yes. There's a bed, a desk and a washing machine.
Can I go and look at it now?
Of course, let's go right now.
g: 如果 A，就 B means "if A, then B".
如果下雨，我们就不去了。
If it rains, we won't go.
离 measures distance between two places or times.
My home is close to school.
q: How far is the flat from the subway?
How much is the rent if you rent for a year?

L.su: A shopper tries on a coat.
ss: Welcome. What would you like to buy?
I'd like to look at that black coat.
Sure. What size do you wear?
I wear medium. Can I try it on?
Of course. The fitting room is over there.
It's a bit big. Do you have a smaller one?
Yes, please wait a moment. How about this one?
This one fits well. How much is it?
It was three hundred yuan, now there's twenty percent off: two hundred and forty.
OK, I'll take this one. Can I pay by phone?
g: 有点儿 vs 一点儿
有点儿 goes before an adjective, 一点儿 goes after it: 大一点儿 (a bit bigger).
Please speak a bit more slowly.
打八折 means 20% off: the number says how many tenths of the price you still pay (八 = 80%).
This piece of clothing is 10% off.
q: What does Mary want to buy?
What is the problem with the first coat?

L.su: A young graduate is interviewed for her first office job.
ss: Please sit down. First, tell us a bit about yourself.
My name is Zhang Xue. I graduated from Peking University last year, majoring in journalism.
Why do you want to work at our company?
Because I have always loved writing, and your magazine is very well known.
Do you have any previous work experience?
At university I did a six-month internship at a newspaper.
What do you think your strengths are?
I am careful in my work, and I am willing to learn new things.
Good. We will call you next week.
Thank you for giving me this opportunity.
g: 为什么 asks the reason. Answer with 因为.
I am willing to help you.
q: When will the company call her?

L.su: A traveller checks in and asks about breakfast.
ss: Hello, welcome. Do you have a reservation?
Yes, my name is Tom. I booked two nights.
Fine, please show me your passport.
Here you are. Can I get online in the room?
Yes. The wifi password is on this card.
What time does breakfast start?
From half past six to nine in the morning, on the second floor.
I need to leave early tomorrow. Can you call a taxi for me?
No problem. Your room is 508, and the lift is on the right.
g: 帮 + person + verb means "help someone do something".
从 A 到 B marks a start and an end, in time or space.
I work from nine to five.
q: How many nights did Tom book?
What does Tom ask the clerk to do?

L.te: The Kitten Looks for a Friend
L.su: A lonely white cat tries to make friends with a little bird.
ss: There was a little white cat that lived in a big house.
Every day it played alone. It had no friends.
One day, it saw a little bird outside the window.
"Hello! Can you play with me?" the kitten asked.
The bird said, "I'm a little afraid of you. Will you eat me?"
The kitten smiled. "I don't eat birds. I only eat fish. I want to be your friend."
The bird thought for a moment, then flew to the window.
From that day on, they played together every day.
The kitten was no longer alone.
g: 了 shows that an action has been completed.
都 means "all" or "always" and goes before the verb.
不再 means "no longer / not any more".
从 + time + 起 means "starting from".
From today on, I will read every day.
q: Why is the bird nervous at first?
It is afraid the cat will eat it
What does the cat say it eats?

L.su: A tourist asks a local how to get to the Summer Palace.
ss: Excuse me, how do I get to the Summer Palace?
You can take the subway. First take Line 4 to Xiyuan Station.
How long does it take?
About forty minutes.
Where do I buy a ticket?
You can use your phone, or buy at the machine in the station.
Do I need to change trains on the way?
No, just stay on until Xiyuan Station.
Thank you so much!
You're welcome. Have a good time!
g: 怎么 + verb asks how to do something.
How do you write this character?
一直 means "straight on" or "all the time".
q: Where does the tourist want to go?
How long does the trip take?
Does the tourist need to change trains?

L.su: A funny description of a lazy cat.
ss: We have a cat called "Mimi", who is three years old this year.
Mimi is white with blue eyes, and she is very pretty.
She loves sleeping and sleeps fifteen hours a day.
In the morning she sleeps by the window, in the afternoon on the sofa, and at night on my bed.
But as soon as I take out the cat food, she wakes up at once.
Sometimes she is very cute too, and comes to the door when I get home.
All of us in the family love Mimi.
g: 只要 A 就 B means "as long as A, then B".
As long as you try hard, you can learn well.
一天 + 要 + amount tells how much someone does or needs per day.
I walk ten thousand steps a day.
q: What makes her wake up at once?

L.su: A friend phones to ask about the weekend.
ss: Hello, is that Xiao Wang? This is Li Hua.
Hi, Li Hua! What's up?
Do you have time this weekend? I'd like to go hiking.
I have to work on Saturday. Sunday is fine.
Great! Let's meet at the subway station at eight in the morning.
Do we need to bring anything?
A bottle of water and a little food is enough.
OK, see you tomorrow!
g: One cup of coffee will do.
想 + verb says what you would like to do.
q: What does Li Hua want to do?
Why can't Xiao Wang go on Saturday?

L.su: A girl describes her best friend at school.
ss: I have a good friend. Her name is Anna.
Anna is my classmate. She is American.
She speaks Chinese very well.
She has a little dog. The dog's name is "Doudou".
Every day we go to school together and go home together.
On Saturdays we often go to her home to play.
The food her mother cooks is very tasty.
g: Verb + 得 + adjective tells how well someone does something.
q: When do they often go to her home?

L.su: A boy tells what sports he and his family like.
ss: I like sports.
I like playing football best.
On Sunday mornings I often play football with my friends at school.
My father likes playing basketball, and he plays very well.
My mother does not like sports. She likes reading.
My older sister can swim. She goes swimming twice a week.
What sports do you like?
g: 喜欢 can be followed by a verb to say what you like doing.
最 means "most" and goes before the word it describes.
q: Which sport does the boy like best?
What does the mother like to do?
How often does the older sister go swimming?

L.te: The Benefits of Getting Up Early
L.su: A writer explains why she changed her morning habits.
ss: I used to love sleeping in, and got up every day only when I was nearly late.
Later I heard from a friend that getting up early is good for your health, so I decided to try.
I put the alarm clock far away, so I couldn't go back to sleep.
For the first few days I wasn't used to it, and had no energy all day.
But after two weeks I found that the morning is especially quiet, and nobody disturbs me.
I can go for a run first, then eat breakfast slowly, and even read for half an hour.
Now my mood is good every morning.
g: 以前 and 后来 contrast how things were and how they became.
以前他不爱运动，后来爱上了跑步。
He used to dislike sport, but later fell in love with running.
才 means "only then" and shows something happens later than expected.
He didn't get up until ten.
q: What kind of person was the writer before?
Where did she put the alarm clock?
What did she find after two weeks?

L.su: Friends decide what to order for dinner.
ss: This restaurant's fish is famous. Let's order one.
I'm not good with spicy food. Are there any dishes that aren't spicy?
Yes, stir-fried greens and tomato and egg soup are not spicy.
Then we'll have a fish, a vegetable dish and a bowl of soup.
What staple would you like? Rice or noodles?
Two bowls of rice.
And two bottles of beer too.
You forgot, we have to drive this afternoon, so we can't drink.
Right. Then two glasses of juice.
g: 都 means "all" or "both" and goes before the verb or adjective.
It is not very cold today.
q: What is famous in this restaurant?
What do they drink in the end?

L.su: A student visits the doctor with a cold.
ss: Hello, where do you not feel well?
I have a headache and a bit of a fever.
Do you cough?
Yes. I didn't sleep well last night.
Let me take a look. Your throat is a bit red.
Is it a cold?
Yes, you have a cold. This is medicine. Take it three times a day, two tablets each time.
Can I go to class?
It's best to rest at home for two days and drink more water.
All right, thank you, doctor.
g: Time words and counts tell how often you do something: 一天 + verb + number + 次.
I drink three glasses of water a day.
最好 means "had better" and is used to give a suggestion.
You had better go to bed early.
q: How often should he take the medicine?
Rest at home and drink water

L.su: A taxi ride turns into a long wait.
ss: Driver, why are there so many cars ahead?
It's Friday, lots of people are leaving work, and on top of that it's raining.
I have an important meeting at eight, and it's already half past seven.
Don't worry. Let me try another road.
OK. Is this road usually jammed?
Not often. It's just that there's an accident ahead today.
Then I'd better take the subway. Please stop here.
Fine. Get out and walk fifty metres to the right, and you'll find the station.
Thanks. How much?
g: Two adjectives joined by 又 describe a state: 又渴又累 "both thirsty and tired".
He is both hungry and tired.
还是 suggests the better choice after thinking.
It's too expensive; I'd better not buy it.
q: Why is there so much traffic?
Rush hour, rain and an accident
What time is the passenger's meeting?
What does the passenger decide to do?

L.su: Two learners share tips.
ss: Xiaomei, I can never remember my characters. Do you have any good methods?
I think the best way is to write a little every day, not too much at once.
What else?
You can learn radicals first. The meaning of many characters is related to the radical.
For example?
For instance 河, 海 and 游 all have the water radical, so they are all connected with water.
So that's how it is! I didn't know before.
Also, you can watch more Chinese TV and chat with Chinese people more.
Good, I'll start today.
g: 跟 A 有关 means "be related to A".
我喜欢水果，比如苹果和香蕉。
I like fruit, for example apples and bananas.
q: What do 河, 海 and 游 have in common?
Watch Chinese TV and chat with Chinese people

L.su: A traveller's flight is delayed, and she asks at the counter.
ss: Hello, I'd like to ask about the flight to Shanghai. Why hasn't boarding started?
I'm very sorry. Because of the weather, this flight has been delayed.
How long will we wait?
That's not certain yet. Please listen for announcements.
I have an important meeting this afternoon. Can I change my ticket?
Yes, but only to the next flight, depending on whether there are free seats.
Then please check for me.
Yes, the 2:30 flight has seats. I've changed it for you.
Thank you so much!
g: 由于 means "because of" and is formal.
Because of rain the match was cancelled.
要看 + a clause tells that the result depends on a condition, often a 有没有 or A不A question.
去不去要看天气好不好。
Whether we go depends on the weather.

L.su: A traveller gets lost in Chengdu and is helped by a kind stranger.
ss: Last month I travelled alone to Chengdu.
That afternoon I wanted to go to a famous hotpot restaurant, but while walking I realized I was lost.
My phone had run out of battery, and I hadn't brought a map either.
I stood at the intersection, not knowing whether to go left or right.
Just then an old gentleman walked over and asked me with a smile, "Young man, do you need help?"
I told him I wanted to go to that hotpot restaurant. He thought for a moment and said, "Walk straight for two hundred meters, then turn right, and you'll see it."
I thanked him, followed his directions, and sure enough I found it very quickly.
The hotpot that evening was delicious, but what I remember most is still the old gentleman's smile.
g: 着 after a verb shows an ongoing state or the manner of an action. Doubling it (走着走着) means "while walking along…".
往 means "toward". Use it with directions: 往左, 往前.
就 connects two actions and suggests the second follows soon or easily after the first.
Go straight and you'll see it.
Besides "or" in questions, 还是 can mean "still / after all" in statements.
我最难忘的，还是他的笑容。
What I remember most is still his smile.
q: Why did the narrator get lost?
The phone had no battery and there was no map
What directions did the old man give?
Straight for 200 meters, then turn right
What did the narrator remember most?

L.s: Retelling of an Aesop fable (public domain)
L.su: A thirsty crow finds a clever way to reach the water.
ss: In summer the weather was hot. A crow had flown for a long time and was both thirsty and tired.
It saw a bottle by the road with a little water in it.
But the bottle was tall, the water was low, and the crow's beak couldn't reach it.
The crow thought for a long time but could not think of a good way.
Suddenly it saw many small stones nearby.
It thought: if I put stones into the bottle, the water will rise.
So the crow dropped the stones into the bottle one by one.
The water rose higher and higher, and at last the crow was able to drink.
g: 越来越 + adjective means "more and more".
The weather is getting hotter and hotter.
又 A 又 B joins two qualities at the same time.
This dish is both tasty and cheap.
q: Why could the crow not drink at first?
The bottle was tall and the water low
What did the crow put into the bottle?

L.su: A manager gives a junior colleague advice about planning her day.
ss: Manager, lately I always feel I don't have enough time. I work overtime every day yet the work isn't finished.
Have you tried ranking your tasks by importance?
No, I usually just do whatever comes to mind.
That makes it easy to be distracted by small things. Each morning you can first make a list and put the three most important things first.
What about the less important things?
You can handle them together in the afternoon, or pass them to someone else.
But colleagues often ask me for help and I feel awkward refusing.
Helping others is good, but learn to say "no" appropriately. You can tell them you'll help after finishing what's at hand.
Understood. I'll try it right away.
g: 手头的事 means "the matter at hand".
I have lots of work in hand.
q: She works overtime but cannot finish
What should she do when colleagues ask for help?
Say no politely and help later

L.su: Xiaomei talks to a rental agent and negotiates the monthly rent.
ss: Hello, I'd like to rent a two-bedroom flat. May I ask whether there is one nearby?
Yes. This one is very close to the subway station, only five minutes on foot. It's 4,500 a month.
The price is a little high. Could it be a bit cheaper?
The landlord says that if you pay six months of rent at once, it can be two hundred yuan cheaper per month.
In that case it's 4,300 a month. I can think about it.
No problem. Would you like to go and have a look at the flat now?
Okay, sorry to trouble you to lead the way.
g: 离 means "(distance) from". The pattern is A + 离 + B + distance word.
The school is very close to my home.
Verb + 不 + Verb is another way to ask a yes/no question and offers both choices.
"if … then …". In speech 如果 is often dropped and 就 carries the meaning alone.
If it rains, we won't go.
一下 softens a verb: "do it for a moment / have a quick go".
q: Why might Xiaomei like the flat?
It is close to the subway
How can she get a lower monthly rent?
By paying six months at once
What would her monthly rent be then?

L.su: An introduction to the Chinese habit of drinking tea.
ss: Chinese people love drinking tea, and have done so for thousands of years.
Common teas include green tea, black tea and oolong tea.
Green tea is the freshest, and southerners particularly like it.
When drinking tea, the host will first pour tea for the guests.
The guest taps the table lightly with their fingers to say "thank you".
Many older people go to a teahouse every morning to drink tea and chat.
Drinking tea is not only good for the body, but also calms people down.
g: 一边 A 一边 B means doing two things at the same time.
他一边走路一边听音乐。
He walks while listening to music.
不但 A 还 B means "not only A but also B".
She is not only pretty but also smart.
q: Which tea do southerners especially like?
How does a guest say thank you?
Where do many older people go in the morning?

L.s: Retelling of an Aesop fable (public domain)
L.su: A shepherd boy tells a lie one time too many.
ss: Long ago there was a little boy who looked after sheep on the hill every day.
He thought looking after sheep every day was very boring.
One day he thought: Let me play a joke.
He shouted loudly, "The wolf is coming! The wolf is coming!"
The people at the foot of the hill heard it and at once ran up the hill carrying whatever they had.
But there was no wolf on the hill. The boy laughed, "Ha ha, I fooled you all!"
A few days later, the wolf really came.
The boy shouted, "The wolf is coming! Come and help me quickly!"
This time nobody believed him.
In the end, all his sheep were eaten by the wolf.
g: 被 turns a sentence around: the thing that gets acted on comes first.
My book was taken away by my friend.
q: What did the boy do for fun?
Why did nobody help him the second time?
What happened to the sheep in the end?

L.s: Retelling of a classical story (Liezi, public domain)
L.te: The Foolish Old Man Moves the Mountains
L.su: An old man's determination to move two mountains.
ss: Long ago there was an old man named Yugong, nearly ninety years old.
In front of his house stood two great mountains, making it hard to leave; he had to take a long detour.
One day Yugong said to his family, "Shall we dig these two mountains flat together?"
Everyone agreed, but his wife worried, "Such big mountains, where will the rocks go?"
Yugong said, "We can carry them to the seashore."
When the neighbour Zhisou heard, he laughed, "You're so old you can't even pull up a blade of grass. And you want to move mountains?"
Yugong replied, "When I die there is my son; when he dies there is a grandson. Generations will never run out, but the mountain won't grow any higher."
The gods were moved by him and sent people to carry the two mountains away.
g: 连 A 都 B means "even A".
q: Where did he plan to carry the rocks?

L.te: The Little Dog Looks for a Bone
L.su: A little dog cannot find his bone, until a bird helps him.
ss: A little dog had a bone.
He liked this bone very much and did not want to give it to anyone.
In the afternoon he put the bone under a tree, and then went to drink water.
When he came back, the bone was gone!
The little dog was very sad. He searched everywhere but could not find it.
At that moment a little bird said, "I saw it. The kitten took it away."
The little dog went to find the kitten. The kitten said, "I'm sorry. I thought it was mine."
The kitten gave the bone back to the little dog, and they became good friends.
g: Verb + 不 + result means "cannot do it".
把 moves the object before the verb: it tells what is done to the thing.
I put the book on the table.
q: Where did the dog put the bone?

L.te: I Want to Learn to Cook
L.su: A student asks his mother to teach him cooking.
ss: Mum, I want to learn to cook. Can you teach me?
Why do you suddenly want to learn cooking?
Next month I'm going to university in another city. If I can't cook, I'll have to eat takeaway every day.
Good idea. Let's start with the simplest: scrambled eggs with tomatoes.
What do we need?
Two tomatoes, three eggs, and a little oil and salt.
What goes in first?
Fry the eggs first. When they're done, put them aside and fry the tomatoes.
And finally put the eggs back in, right?
Right, you learn fast!
g: ……的话 turns the first part into a condition.
不快点儿的话，我们会迟到。
If we don't hurry, we'll be late.
只能 means "can only" or "have no choice but to".
下雨了，我们只能在家看电视。
It's raining, so we can only watch TV at home.
q: Why does David want to learn cooking?
He will study in another city
What is the first dish he learns?

L.su: An article encouraging people to bring their own shopping bags.
ss: In the past, when we went shopping at the supermarket, the staff always gave us many plastic bags.
These plastic bags are thrown away after one use, but they will not disappear for hundreds of years.
They pollute rivers and soil, and they hurt animals.
Now many countries have begun to charge for them to encourage people to bring their own shopping bags.
I think this is a good method.
I always keep a cloth bag in my backpack, and I can use it whenever I shop.
If everyone uses one fewer plastic bag, the earth will be a little cleaner.
g: 会 is also used to say what will happen.
q: They stay for hundreds of years
What have many countries started to do?
What does the writer keep in the bag?

L.su: Friends help a colleague move to a new flat.
ss: Lao Zhang, have you packed everything?
Almost. I have so many books, I filled more than ten boxes.
What's in this big box? It's so heavy!
My old books. I can't bear to throw them away.
The removal van has arrived. Let's carry the big things down first.
What about the sofa? The door is so narrow it might not fit through.
Take the legs off and try.
Done, it's out! Which floor is the new place on?
The sixth floor, no lift. I'm really sorry to trouble you today.
Don't mention it. Just treat us to dinner tonight.
g: 舍不得 means "reluctant to part with".
这么 + adjective emphasises the degree.
q: What does Lao Zhang have too many of?
Why is the sofa a problem?
What is Lao Zhang's new home like?

L.su: Tidying up, the narrator finds a letter from their grandmother and decides to call her.
ss: While tidying my room, I found an old letter in the bottom drawer of my desk.
The envelope had already turned yellow, but the handwriting on it was still clear. It was written to me by my grandma.
Ten years ago, when I first left home for university in another city, Grandma was reluctant to see me go, yet she said nothing and just silently helped me pack.
The letter said: "Child, don't worry about home. Just study hard, and when you run into difficulties, believe in yourself."
As I read on, my eyes grew moist. All these years I have always been busy with work and rarely come home to see her.
I immediately picked up my phone and called Grandma.
At the other end of the line, her voice was as gentle as ever: "How come you suddenly thought of me?"
I said with a smile, "Grandma, this weekend I'm coming back to see you. I'll bring the pastries you love most."
g: 是…的 puts the focus on who, when, where or how something happened. It is used for events that are already finished.
This letter was written by Grandma.
却 means "yet / however" and marks a contrast with what you would expect. It goes after the subject.
He's tired, yet doesn't want to rest.
Repeating a verb with 着 means "while doing it… (something else happens)".
舍不得 means "to be reluctant to part with" or "to hate to do something".
q: How did the narrator feel while reading it?
What does the narrator promise at the end?
To visit this weekend and bring pastries
How long ago did the narrator leave for university?

L.su: Why a good night's sleep matters.
ss: Many people think sleeping is a waste of time, so they often stay up late working or playing on their phones.
In fact, sleep is very important for health.
Doctors say adults should ideally sleep seven to eight hours a day.
If you sleep too little, you feel low on energy and fall ill easily.
Long-term lack of sleep also affects memory and lowers efficiency in study and work.
To sleep well, avoid coffee in the evening and don't look at your phone for an hour before bed.
Also, keeping the room quiet and dark helps.
g: 其实 introduces the real situation.
容易 + verb means "easy to / likely to".
It's easy to catch cold in winter.
q: How many hours should adults sleep?
What can lack of sleep affect?
What should you avoid before bed?

L.su: A father and daughter disagree about her university subject.
ss: Xiaoyu, have you filled in your university choices?
I have. My first choice is art and design.
Art and design? Is it easy to find a job after graduating in that?
Dad, many companies need designers now. And I really love drawing.
I'm not saying you can't draw. I just hope you pick a more stable major, like accounting or law.
But I have no interest in numbers at all.
Interest can be developed slowly.
If I did things I don't like every day, how could I possibly do them well?
You have a point. Let me think about it again.
g: 对 A 有兴趣 means "be interested in A".
I am very interested in music.
一点儿也 + negative means "not at all".
q: What does Xiaoyu want to study?
He thinks it may be hard to find a job
The father says he will think again

L.su: How a Chinese family prepares for the New Year.
ss: Spring Festival is China's biggest holiday, and family members all go home to celebrate together.
Before the New Year, everyone first cleans the house and then buys lots of good food.
Red couplets are pasted on the doors, with good wishes written on them.
On New Year's Eve the family sits together making dumplings and watching TV.
At twelve o'clock, many people outside set off firecrackers.
The children are the happiest, because adults give them red envelopes.
The next day everyone visits relatives and friends to wish them a happy New Year.
g: 先 A 然后 B puts two actions in order.
I wash my hands first and then eat.
因为 gives the reason; 所以 gives the result.
Because it rained, I didn't go.
q: What do families make on New Year's Eve?
What do children get from adults?
What do people stick on the doors?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Han Fei Zi, public domain)
L.te: Marking the Boat to Find the Sword
L.su: A man who loses his sword in a river makes a foolish mark.
ss: A man of Chu was crossing a river by boat.
When the boat reached the middle of the river, he carelessly dropped his sword into the water.
He immediately carved a mark on the side of the boat and said, "My sword fell in right here."
The boat kept moving and soon reached the bank.
The man jumped into the water and searched for his sword at the place he had marked.
He looked for a long time but found nothing.
Others asked him why, and he said, "My sword fell here. How could I not find it?"
He didn't understand that the boat had moved while the sword stayed where it had fallen.
g: 一 A 就 B means "as soon as A, then B".
As soon as he gets home he watches TV.
怎么会 + negative expresses disbelief: "how could it be that...?"
q: Where did he make a mark?

L.su: An interviewer asks a candidate about her strengths and plans.
ss: Please begin with a short self-introduction.
Sure. I graduated from a university in Shanghai, majored in marketing, and worked three years at an advertising company.
Why do you want to leave your previous company?
Mainly I hope for more room to grow. I accumulated a lot of experience there, but promotion opportunities were limited.
What do you think is your greatest strength?
I am good at communication and have a strong sense of responsibility. Last year I led a team to complete an important project and the client was very satisfied.
Then do you have any weaknesses?
Sometimes I demand too much of myself and put pressure on colleagues. But I am learning to adjust.
Good. We will inform you of the result as soon as possible.
g: 她善于表达自己的想法。
She is good at expressing her ideas.
尽快 means "as soon as possible".
Please reply as soon as possible.
q: Why does she want to leave?
What does she say is her weakness?

L.su: How app-based bikes changed short trips in Chinese cities.
ss: A few years ago, many brightly coloured bicycles suddenly appeared in China's big cities.
These bikes belong to no one; anyone can scan a code with a phone and just park by the roadside when finished.
For office workers, shared bikes solved the "last kilometre" problem.
From the subway station to the company is only two kilometres: too far to walk, but not worth taking a taxi.
But shared bikes have also brought new troubles.
Some people park carelessly and block the pavement; some broken bikes are never repaired.
Later the government and companies drew up rules together: park only in marked areas, or you will be fined.
Now the bikes on the street are much tidier.
g: 对 A 来说 means "as far as A is concerned".
q: How do people unlock the bikes?
By scanning a code with a phone
What problem did the bikes solve?
The last kilometre between the subway and work
How are the new rules enforced?
Fines for parking outside marked areas

L.su: Someone who always ordered takeout learns to cook and discovers practice pays off.
ss: I never used to cook. Every day I ordered takeout.
Later I realized takeout was not only expensive but also not very healthy, so I decided to learn to cook myself.
The first time I made tomato and egg stir-fry, I put in too much salt and burnt the eggs as well.
My friend took a bite and said with a smile, "Not bad, just a little salty."
Now I have already learned to make more than ten dishes.
Although I can't really say I cook well, I love this feeling.
Cooking has taught me that as long as you practice more, everything gets easier and easier.
g: "not only … but also …". It links two points that build on each other.
他不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。
He can not only sing, but also dance.
把 moves the object in front of the verb to show what you did to it and what the result was.
I put in too much salt.
"although … but …". Unlike English, Chinese normally uses both words.
越来越 + adjective means "more and more …".
The weather is getting colder and colder.
q: Why did the writer start learning to cook?
Takeout is expensive and not very healthy
What went wrong the first time?
Too much salt and burnt eggs
What did the friend say about the dish?
Not bad, just a little salty

L.su: A customer complains to customer service about a wrong order.
ss: Hello, last week I bought a blue sweater in your shop, but the one I received is grey.
I'm very sorry for the inconvenience. May I ask your order number?
Here: 123456. I've contacted you twice already and nobody has replied.
I'm truly sorry. We've had too many orders lately and are a little slow.
I don't want the grey one. Can I return it?
Of course. Just apply for a return on your phone; the courier will collect it from your door, and we cover the shipping.
And how long will the refund take?
After we receive the item it normally takes three to five working days. To apologise, we'll also send you a coupon.
All right, thanks for your patience.
g: 由 + party + 承担 means "to be borne by".
I usually get up at seven.
q: What was wrong with the order?
How long does the refund take?

L.su: Tea is more than a drink in China: it shows respect, varies by region, and calms the mind.
ss: In China, tea is not just a kind of drink, but even more a way of life.
When a guest comes to someone's home, the host always pours a cup of tea first. This shows welcome and respect.
Different places like different teas. Southerners love green tea, northerners like jasmine tea, whereas Cantonese people are used to eating dim sum while drinking tea.
Research shows that drinking tea in moderation is good for your health, for example it can help people relax.
However, the greatest charm of tea may still be the kind of calm it brings.
So a cup of tea is often not just for quenching thirst.
g: "not just … but even more …". It lifts a topic to a bigger idea.
这不只是工作，更是生活。
This is not just work, but a way of life.
边 + verb … 边 + verb means doing two actions at the same time.
He listens to music while walking.
比如 introduces an example: "for example".
I like fruit, for example apples.
而 contrasts two groups or ideas: "whereas".
他喜欢茶，而我喜欢咖啡。
He likes tea, whereas I like coffee.
q: What does pouring tea for a guest show?
According to the article, what can tea in moderation help with?

L.su: How a village changed in twenty years.
ss: Twenty years ago my hometown was a quiet, isolated village with just one dirt road, almost impassable on rainy days.
Most young people went to work in the cities, leaving only the old and the children.
In recent years, with the government's growing investment in rural areas, the village has changed greatly.
The road was repaired, the internet arrived, and farmers can sell their fruit and vegetables online.
Some young people saw opportunities and chose to come back and start businesses, opening guesthouses and farm restaurants.
The village primary school has reopened, and children no longer need to walk many miles to school.
Of course, change has also brought new problems such as environmental protection and the passing on of traditional culture.
But I believe that if we all work together, tomorrow will be better for my hometown.
g: 随着年龄的增长，他变得更成熟了。
As he grew older, he became more mature.
q: What was the village like twenty years ago?
What do farmers now do online?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Han Fei Zi, public domain)
L.su: A merchant's boast about his spear and shield is easily tested.
ss: Long ago a man in the state of Chu was selling spears and shields in the street.
First he held up a shield and shouted, "My shield is the strongest in the world. Nothing can pierce it!"
Then he held up a spear and said, "My spear is the sharpest in the world. It can pierce anything!"
A man nearby asked him, "What would happen if you used your spear to pierce your shield?"
The seller opened his mouth but could not say a word.
The people around him laughed, and he had to take his things and go home.
Later people used "contradicting oneself" to describe talking or acting inconsistently.
g: 什么 + noun + 都 means "any ... at all".
I like to eat any dish.
只好 means "have no choice but to".
The car broke down, so we had to walk.
q: What question did the bystander ask?
What if the spear pierces the shield
What does 自相矛盾 describe?
Saying things that contradict each other

L.su: A traveller's diary from the ancient capital.
ss: On the first day we visited the Terracotta Army.
The Terracotta Army is more than two thousand years old, and every soldier's face is different.
On the second day we climbed Xi'an's ancient city wall and rode bicycles all the way around.
Looking down from the wall, we could see the old city and the new city in front of us.
In the evening we went to the Muslim Quarter for snacks: lamb stew with bread, cold noodles and meat buns.
On the third day we went to the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and watched the musical fountain in the square.
Three days was too short. We will definitely come again.
g: 已经 ... 了 shows a state that has been reached.
q: What did they see on the first day?
How did they go round the city wall?

L.s: Retelling of history (Sima Qian, public domain)
L.su: The teacher who spent thirteen years looking for a ruler who would listen.
ss: Confucius was ancient China's greatest thinker and educator, born in the state of Lu.
As a young man he held office in Lu, but his political ideas were not valued by the ruler.
At fifty-five Confucius left Lu with a group of students and began to travel among the states.
They visited many states hoping to find a ruler willing to practise benevolent government.
On the way they met war, hunger and danger; once they were even besieged for seven days without food.
The students were discouraged, but Confucius still played the zither and sang in the room.
More than ten years later, Confucius returned home and put his energy into teaching and editing ancient classics.
It is said he had three thousand students, seventy-two of them outstanding.
His thought has had a profound influence on the culture of China and even East Asia.
g: 甚至 means "even" and adds an extreme example.
He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.
乃至 means "and even" and raises the scale.
这件事影响了全国乃至世界。
This affected the whole country and even the world.
q: At what age did Confucius leave Lu?
A ruler willing to practise benevolent government
How did he react to hardship?
He kept playing music and singing

L.su: An overview of regional cooking in China.
ss: China is big and eating habits differ greatly from region to region, hence the saying "the eight great cuisines".
Sichuan cuisine is the food of Sichuan, known for being numbing and spicy, and many foreigners love it.
Cantonese cuisine comes from Guangdong. It emphasises freshness and its flavours are comparatively light.
Shandong cuisine, the representative of northern food, often uses stir-frying and braising.
Jiangsu and Zhejiang cuisines are both from the south of the Yangtze; the dishes look beautiful and the taste leans sweet.
In addition there are Hunan, Fujian and Anhui cuisines.
If someone tried all eight cuisines, it would probably take several years.
q: Which cuisine is numbing and spicy?
Which region is the northern representative?

L.s: Retelling of an Aesop fable (public domain)
L.su: A hungry fox cannot reach the grapes and pretends he doesn't want them.
ss: A fox had walked all day and was hungry and thirsty.
He saw a grape vine ahead, with bunches of purple grapes hanging from it.
"They look delicious!" said the fox.
But the grapes hung high. He jumped once and could not reach them.
He jumped again and still could not reach them.
He jumped many times and was so tired that he sat on the ground.
He looked at the grapes and said, "These grapes must be sour. I don't want them anyway."
Then he slowly walked away.
g: Verb/adjective + 得 + result tells how strong the action was.
He was so tired he fell asleep.
q: Why could he not get them?
What did the fox say in the end?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Zhuangzi, public domain)
L.te: The Frog at the Bottom of the Well
L.su: A frog thinks his well is the whole world until a turtle visits.
ss: There was a frog who had always lived in a shallow well.
Every day he swam and hopped about in the well, and thought he was the happiest creature in the world.
One day a big sea turtle from the Eastern Sea passed by.
The frog said proudly to the turtle, "Look, how comfortable my home is! Come down and sit a while!"
The turtle wanted to go down, but his legs were too big to fit.
He said to the frog, "Have you seen the sea? It is thousands of miles wide and thousands of feet deep."
The frog heard this and said nothing. Only then did he realise his little well was tiny compared with the sea.
g: 听了他的话，我这才明白。
Only after hearing him did I understand.
Verb + 来 + verb + 去 shows an action repeated in different directions.
q: Why could the turtle not go down?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Zhan Guo Ce, public domain)
L.su: A drawing contest teaches that more is not always better.
ss: Several men of Chu were drinking together, but there was only one jug, not enough for everyone.
Someone said, "Let's have a snake-drawing contest. Whoever finishes first gets the jug."
Everyone bent down and began to draw. One man drew fastest and finished in no time.
He picked up the jug, saw the others still drawing, and said proudly, "You're too slow. I even have time to add feet to the snake!"
Before he could finish, another man had already completed his drawing.
That man snatched the jug and said, "Snakes have no feet to begin with. What you drew isn't a snake."
Having said this, he drank all the wine in the jug.
Later people used "drawing feet on a snake" to mean that doing something unnecessary only spoils things.
g: 本来 means "originally" or "in the first place".
我本来想去，后来下雨了。
I originally wanted to go, but then it rained.
反而 shows the result is the opposite of what you expect.
他吃了药，病反而更重了。
He took medicine and got worse instead.
q: Why did the first man lose?
He added feet to the snake
Doing unnecessary things spoils the result

L.s: Retelling of an Aesop fable (public domain)
L.su: A slow tortoise beats a fast but careless hare.
ss: There was a hare who ran very fast and often said other animals were too slow.
The tortoise said, "Let's have a race!"
The hare laughed, "You? You walk so slowly. How could you beat me?"
The race began, and soon the hare was far ahead.
He looked back and the tortoise was still far away.
"I'll take a nap first, and run again when he comes," thought the hare.
The tortoise kept going forward without resting.
When the hare woke up, the tortoise was almost at the finish line.
The hare ran with all his might, but it was too late. The tortoise had won.
g: A 比 B + adjective compares two things.
一直 shows a continuing action without stopping.
He has been studying all the time.
q: What did the tortoise do during the race?
What is the lesson of the story?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Lüshi Chunqiu, public domain)
L.te: Covering One's Ears to Steal the Bell
L.su: A thief thinks that if he cannot hear, nobody else can.
ss: Long ago a thief saw a beautiful big bell hanging at the door of a house.
He badly wanted to take it, but when he touched it, the bell rang "ding-dong, ding-dong".
He thought, "People will hear this. What should I do?"
After thinking for a while, he covered his ears with both hands.
"I can't hear it any more," he thought, "so others surely can't either."
So he went to take the bell without worry.
The bell rang. The owner heard it, ran out at once and caught the thief.
This story mocks people who deceive themselves.
q: What did the thief want to steal?
What did he do to avoid being heard?
What does the story make fun of?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Mencius, public domain)
L.su: An impatient farmer ruins his crop trying to help it grow.
ss: In the state of Song a farmer had planted some seedlings and went to look at them every day.
He felt they grew too slowly and was very anxious.
One day he thought of a "good idea": pull each seedling up a little.
He worked from morning till night and became drenched in sweat.
Back home he said happily to his family, "I'm exhausted today, but all the seedlings have grown much taller!"
His son found it strange and ran to the field at once to look.
The seedlings had all withered and died.
The story tells us: follow natural laws when doing things, and don't be too impatient.
g: 从 A V 到 B means doing something from one point to another.
He was busy from morning till night.

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Han Fei Zi, public domain)
L.te: Waiting by the Stump for a Hare
L.su: A farmer stops working because of one lucky accident.
ss: In ancient times there was a farmer in the state of Song who worked hard in his field every day.
One day a hare ran so fast that it crashed head-first into a tree stump at the edge of the field and died.
The farmer got a hare without any effort and was delighted.
From then on he no longer wanted to farm.
Every day he sat beside the stump, waiting for hares to run into it.
But he waited many days and not one hare came.
The weeds in his field grew taller than the crops, and everyone laughed at how foolish he was.
The story tells us: don't treat a stroke of luck as something that will happen every day.
g: 从……以后 marks the starting point of a change.
From then on he ran every day.
A 比 B 还 + adjective means "even more ... than B".
He is even taller than me.
q: It hit a stump and died
It was caught in a net
What did the farmer do after that?
He sat by the stump waiting

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Huainanzi, public domain)
L.te: The Old Man Who Lost His Horse
L.su: Good and bad fortune keep changing places.
ss: An old man lived on the frontier, and everyone called him "Old Man Sai".
One day his horse ran off into the territory of the northern tribes. Neighbours all came to comfort him.
But Sai said, "This may not be a bad thing."
A few months later the horse returned with a fine horse.
The neighbours all came to congratulate him, and Sai said, "This may not be a good thing either."
Later Sai's son rode the new horse, fell off carelessly and broke his leg.
A year later war broke out and young men were called to fight, and many died.
Sai's son, because of his bad leg, was not called up, and his life was saved.
g: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
因为 gives a reason for a result that did not happen.
He didn't come because of the rain.
q: What happened to the old man's horse first?
How did the son break his leg?
He fell from the new horse
Why was the son saved from war?

L.su: Practical advice for handling pressure at work and school.
ss: Stress is almost part of modern life. A moderate amount of it can motivate us, but too much harms our health.
Facing stress, first learn to accept it rather than simply avoid it.
Second, you can divide a big task into small goals and complete them step by step, which feels much lighter.
Exercise is also a good way to relieve stress; even half an hour of walking a day will improve your mood.
In addition, getting enough sleep and drinking less coffee give the body more energy.
Finally, don't hide all your problems inside; talk to family and friends, and you will often find things aren't as bad as imagined.
If stress cannot be relieved for a long time, you should seek professional help in good time.
g: A 而不是 B means "A, not B".
我要的是自由，而不是金钱。
What I want is freedom, not money.
哪怕 A 也 B means "even if A, still B".
Even if it rains I'll go.
q: How can big tasks feel easier?
By splitting them into small goals
What should you do if stress lasts long?

L.s: Retelling of a classical idiom story (Zhan Guo Ce, public domain)
L.te: The Fox Borrows the Tiger's Might
L.su: A clever fox saves himself by using a tiger's fearsome reputation.
ss: A tiger in the forest was hungry and caught a fox.
The fox was clever. He said to the tiger, "You wouldn't dare eat me! The Heavenly Emperor sent me to govern the forest."
The tiger did not believe it. The fox said, "If you don't believe me, walk with me and see whether the animals fear me."
So the fox walked in front with the tiger following behind.
The animals in the forest saw them and ran away in fright.
The tiger thought the animals really feared the fox, and let him go.
In fact, what the animals feared was the tiger behind the fox.
Later people used "the fox borrows the tiger's might" to describe borrowing someone's power to scare others.
g: 吓得 + result means "so frightened that ...".
He was so scared he couldn't speak.
q: He was sent to rule the forest
Who were the animals really afraid of?

L.su: Why learning shouldn't stop at graduation.
ss: In the past people thought school was for earning a diploma, and that learning ended with graduation.
But in today's world of faster knowledge turnover, that view is outdated.
Many professional skills become obsolete within a few years, and without continued study one is easily eliminated by the times.
Lifelong learning is not only to adapt to work but even more to enrich one's inner world.
Now there are plenty of online courses, and people can use fragments of time to learn new things anywhere, anytime.
What matters is not how fast you learn but whether you keep your curiosity and form the habit of perseverance.
As an old saying goes, "Live until old, learn until old."
g: 不仅 A 更 B means "not only A, but even more B".
He is not only clever but even more diligent.
随时随地 is a set phrase: "anytime, anywhere".
手机让我们随时随地都能联系。
Phones let us keep in touch anytime, anywhere.
q: What is outdated according to the text?
What can people use to study?
What does the old saying mean?

L.s: Tang poem by Wang Zhihuan (public domain)
L.su: Wang Zhihuan climbs a tower and reaches for a wider view.
ss: The white sun sinks behind the hills;
the Yellow River flows into the sea.
To see a thousand miles farther,
climb one more storey up the tower.
q: What does the poet want to see?
What advice does the last line give?
Climb higher for a wider view

L.s: Tang poem by Luo Binwang (public domain)
L.su: A child-poet describes geese on a clear pond.
ss: Goose, goose, goose,
with a curved neck you sing to the sky.
White feathers float on green water;
red webbed feet paddle the clear waves.
q: With its neck curved to the sky

L.s: Tang poem by Meng Haoran (public domain)
L.su: Meng Haoran wakes to birdsong and wonders how many blossoms fell in the night rain.
ss: Sleeping in spring, I don't notice the dawn;
everywhere I hear birds singing.
Last night came the sound of wind and rain;
how many flowers fell, who knows?
q: What does the poet not notice?
What does he wonder at the end?

L.s: Tang poem by Li Bai (public domain)
L.su: Li Bai, lying awake in the moonlight, thinks of his hometown.
ss: Before my bed, the bright moonlight,
I wonder if it is frost upon the ground.
I raise my head to gaze at the bright moon,
I lower my head and think of home.
q: What does the poet see before his bed?
What does the poet mistake the light for?
What does he feel at the end?

L.s: Tang poem by Li Bai (public domain)
L.su: Li Bai thanks a friend who sings a farewell on the shore.
ss: Li Bai is about to leave by boat,
when suddenly he hears stamping songs on the bank.
Peach Blossom Pool is a thousand feet deep,
yet it is no deeper than Wang Lun's feeling in seeing me off.
q: What is compared with the pool?

L.su: Traditional first lessons about human nature and education.
ss: At the beginning, human nature is good.
By nature people are alike; through habit they grow apart.
If they are not taught, their nature changes.
The way of teaching values focus.
Long ago Mencius's mother chose her neighbours carefully.
When her son would not study, she cut the cloth on her loom.
q: According to the opening, human nature at birth is ...

L.s: Tang poem by Li Shen (public domain)
L.su: Li Shen reminds us how hard farmers work for each grain of rice.
ss: Hoeing the seedlings at noon,
sweat drips onto the soil below.
Who knows that the food in our bowls,
every single grain, comes from hard labour?

L.te: A Story from the Night Market
L.su: A tofu-pudding seller who never raises his prices gives a homesick customer a bowl he cannot forget.
ss: At six in the early evening, Old Zhou pushed his little cart to the night market as usual.
What he sold was the tofu pudding he made himself, only five yuan a bowl, and in twenty years he had never raised the price.
Someone advised him, "Everything has gone up in price now. You should raise yours a little too."
Old Zhou just shook his head: "The people who come are all familiar faces. If I raised the price, they'd feel too awkward to come."
That night, a young man stood in front of the stall for a long time.
He said that when he was little, every day after school his mother would bring him here for a bowl of tofu pudding.
Later he went abroad to work, and he hadn't been back in ten years.
Old Zhou was stunned for a moment, then handed him a steaming bowl of tofu pudding and said, "This bowl is on the house."
The young man lowered his head and took a mouthful, and his eyes suddenly turned red — the taste was, unexpectedly, exactly the same as in his memory.
g: 像 A 一样 means "like / the same as A".
He got up early, as usual.
从没 + verb + 过 means "never (have done)". 过 marks past experience.
I have never been to Beijing.
竟然 expresses surprise that something is unexpected.
一下 means "briefly"; 一下子 means "all of a sudden".
q: Why has Old Zhou never raised his prices?
He doesn't want his regulars to feel awkward
What did the young man's mother do when he was little?
She took him for tofu pudding after school
How did the young man react after tasting it?
His eyes reddened because it tasted just like his memory
He complained it was too sweet
He asked for his money back
How long had the young man been away?

L.su: Why people feel alone in crowded places.
ss: Walking down a big-city street you see thousands of people, yet many feel lonely.
This sounds contradictory but is actually not strange.
Modern people are under great work pressure, tired after getting home, and have no energy left to socialise with neighbours and friends.
In buildings where they have lived for years, some people don't even know who lives next door.
Although phones and social apps make contact easy, they also reduce face-to-face communication.
Psychologists point out that long-term loneliness not only affects mood but also harms physical health.
To escape loneliness, you might start with small things: greet a neighbour, join community activities, or invite a friend to meet at the weekend.
As long as we are willing to take the first step, we will find that there is plenty of kindness around us.
g: 虽然 A，却 B concedes A but stresses the contrast B.
不妨 means "might as well" and gently suggests an action.
You might as well try this method.
q: What does the article say about big cities?
Many people feel lonely despite crowds
What do psychologists say loneliness can harm?
Start with small acts like greeting neighbours

L.s: Retelling of a classic idiom story (Zhuangzi / Han Feizi, public domain)
L.su: Why doing too much can spoil the job.
ss: A noble of the state of Chu, after sacrificing to his ancestors, gave a pot of wine to several of his retainers.
They discussed: "There's not enough for many but more than enough for one. Let's have a snake-drawing contest — whoever finishes first drinks the wine."
Everyone agreed and squatted on the ground drawing.
One man finished quickly; as he picked up the pot to drink, he looked back and saw the others still bent over their drawings.
He said proudly, "You're too slow; I can even add some feet to my snake!"
While he was drawing the feet, another man finished and snatched the pot: "Snakes never had feet — what you've drawn isn't a snake!"
With that, he tilted back his head and drained it all.
Later people used "drawing legs on a snake" to mean doing something superfluous and ruining the matter instead.
g: 画蛇添足 is a chengyu: "do something superfluous that spoils the whole".
这个结尾真是画蛇添足。
This ending is truly gilding the lily.
反而 means "on the contrary; instead".
He took medicine and got worse instead.
q: Why was the winner's snake disqualified?
Doing superfluous things that spoil the result

L.su: An essay on why "slow living" appeals to young city dwellers and how to start.
ss: In recent years, "slow living" has become a topic that many young city dwellers talk about.
In a fast-paced society, people are chased by work and their phones every day, and have almost no time to stop and think about what they truly want.
So-called slow living does not mean doing nothing at all, but learning to leave a little blank space for yourself amid the busyness.
For example, walking home after work rather than squeezing onto the subway; on weekends turning off your phone, carefully cooking a meal, or chatting with your family.
These seemingly ordinary little things can make people feel the texture of life anew.
Of course, slowing down is not easy, because we have long been used to a way of thinking that puts efficiency above all.
But as long as we start with one small thing, perhaps we can slowly find our inner balance again.
g: 被 marks the passive: the subject receives the action. The doer, if named, follows 被.
I got soaked by the rain.
并 before a negative word stresses a correction: "actually not / not at all".
"not A but B". 而不是 A means "rather than A".
他不是不想去，而是没时间。
It's not that he doesn't want to go; he has no time.
"as long as … then …". It names the one condition that is enough.
As long as you work hard, you can succeed.
q: What does slow living really mean, according to the essay?
Leaving some blank space amid a busy life
Which example does the writer give?
Walking home instead of taking the subway
We are used to putting efficiency first
We have too much free time
What does the writer suggest at the end?

L.s: Retelling of a traditional Chinese folk tale
L.te: The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl
L.su: The love story behind the Qixi Festival.
ss: Long ago there was a young man called Niulang. His family was poor and had only an old ox.
The old ox was actually a god from heaven, and it liked Niulang's kindness.
One day the ox said to Niulang, "Tomorrow fairies from heaven will bathe at the river. If you take one of the dresses, you can marry her."
The next day Niulang did what the ox said, and he met the Weaver Girl.
After they married, they lived happily and had a son and a daughter.
But the Queen Mother of Heaven learned of this, became very angry, and took the Weaver Girl back to heaven.
Niulang took the children, wanting to go to heaven to find her.
Then the Queen Mother drew a great river across the sky with a golden hairpin. That is the Milky Way.
The magpies in the sky were moved. Every year on the seventh of July they fly together to form a bridge so Niulang and the Weaver Girl can meet.
g: 其实 means "actually" and introduces the truth that differs from what you might think.
让 + person + verb means "let/make someone do something".
Mother told me to go to bed early.
q: What was the old ox really?
What did the Queen Mother draw in the sky?
Who builds the bridge every year?

L.su: A tenant and a landlord argue over the deposit.
ss: Landlord, I'm moving out next month and would like to discuss the deposit.
According to the contract, the deposit is returned only after inspection.
I understand. But in these two years the flat has been kept very clean.
Clean is clean, but there are some scratches on the wall and the sofa is worn; these all need repair.
Surely these are normal wear and tear? The contract says clearly that natural wear isn't covered by compensation.
Even so, the scratches were clearly man-made.
How about this: we find a neutral party to assess it, each paying half?
Fine, to avoid spoiling our good relations.
g: 免得 means "so as not to; lest".
Take an umbrella lest you get wet.

L.su: How AI is quietly changing work, study and health care.
ss: Ten years ago, artificial intelligence was, for most people, merely a plot in science-fiction films.
Today it has quietly seeped into every corner of our lives: phones understand our speech, cars can drive themselves, and hospitals use it to assist in diagnosing disease.
In education, intelligent software can draw up personalised study plans according to each student's level.
For companies, artificial intelligence can greatly raise efficiency and save costs.
However, technological progress has also brought new worries.
Some worry that many jobs will be replaced by machines, while others worry that personal privacy cannot be guaranteed.
Experts believe the key lies in how to use the technology sensibly rather than simply rejecting it.
Only by establishing sound laws and rules can artificial intelligence truly benefit humankind.
g: 对 A 来说 means "as far as A is concerned".
只有 A 才 B means "only if A, then B".
Only through effort can one succeed.
q: What can AI do for hospitals?
What are two worries people have?
What do experts say is the key?

L.su: Bikes, rides and rooms: how sharing became a business model.
ss: In recent years shared bikes, shared cars and shared power banks have rapidly entered people's lives.
The sharing economy refers to people using internet platforms to temporarily let others use idle goods or services in order to earn income.
For users, being able to enjoy a service without buying it is both convenient and cheap.
For providers, idle resources become extra income.
However, the sharing economy has also met many problems.
In some cities the streets are piled with carelessly parked shared bikes, which both hinder traffic and waste resources.
Some firms collapsed through poor management and broken funding chains, and users' deposits became hard to recover.
Clearly, for the sharing economy to keep developing, effective supervision and a credit system must be established.
g: 既 A 又 B means "both A and B".
这家饭店既便宜又好吃。
This restaurant is both cheap and tasty.
可见 means "it can be seen that".
他没来，可见他不想参加。
He didn't come; clearly he doesn't want to take part.
q: What does the sharing economy let people do?
What problem is mentioned about bikes?
What does the writer say is needed?
Effective supervision and a credit system

L.su: How an ancient trade route connected East and West.
ss: In 138 BC, Zhang Qian, an envoy of the Han dynasty, set out from Chang'an for the Western Regions.
His mission was to unite the Western states against the Xiongnu in the north.
On the way he was captured by the Xiongnu and held for over ten years before finally escaping.
Although he did not complete his original task, he brought back a great deal of information about the Western Regions.
After that, a trade route linking East and West gradually took shape.
Caravans carried Chinese silk, tea and porcelain to the West, and brought back spices, gems and glass.
Besides goods, religion, art and technology also spread along the road: Buddhism entered China, and papermaking reached Europe.
Today the "Silk Road" has become a symbol of cultural exchange and cooperation.
g: The weather is gradually getting cold.
除了 A 也 B means "besides A, also B".
除了英语，他也会说法语。
Besides English, he can also speak French.
q: Where did Zhang Qian start his journey?
What was taken west along the road?

L.s: Tang poem by Du Mu (public domain)
L.su: Du Mu stops his carriage to admire autumn leaves.
ss: Far up the cold mountain a stone path slants;
where white clouds rise, there are homes.
I stop the carriage, loving the maple grove at dusk;
frost-touched leaves are redder than spring flowers.
q: What are redder than spring flowers?

L.s: Tang poem by Du Mu (public domain)
L.su: Du Mu, walking in drizzle, asks a cowherd where to find wine.
ss: At Qingming time the rain falls in drifting threads;
